Let \(n=\prod p_i^{e_i}\). Then
\[
D(110n^3)=(2+3e_2)(2+3e_5)(2+3e_{11})\prod_{p\ne 2,5,11}(3e_p+1)=110.
\]
Each factor must divide \(110=2\cdot5\cdot11\).

For \(p=2,5,11\), the factors are \(\equiv 2\pmod 3\), so they are among \(2,5,11,110\). Their product must divide \(110\), so the only possibility is
\[
(2+3e_2)(2+3e_5)(2+3e_{11})=2\cdot5\cdot11.
\]
Thus \(\{e_2,e_5,e_{11}\}=\{0,1,3\}\), and all other \(e_p=0\).

Now
\[
81n^4=3^4\cdot 2^{4e_2}\cdot 5^{4e_5}\cdot 11^{4e_{11}}.
\]
So its divisor count is
\[
(4+1)(4e_2+1)(4e_5+1)(4e_{11}+1).
\]
Since \(\{e_2,e_5,e_{11}\}=\{0,1,3\}\),
\[
(4e_2+1)(4e_5+1)(4e_{11}+1)=1\cdot5\cdot13=65.
\]
Therefore,
\[
D(81n^4)=5\cdot65=325.
\]

\[
\boxed{325}
\]
